    build() - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalProcessedStream
    Freezes this stage and builds the single-stage CausalTopology, ready to be assembled into a real Kafka Streams Topology once a CausalStreams runtime supplies its props.

    C

    CausalDependencies - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    A producer-stamped set of causal requirements: the positions a consumer must have observed before a record stamped with these dependencies may be delivered.
    CausalDependencies.Builder - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    Builder for CausalDependencies.
    CausalProcessedStream<K,V> - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    A causal stage bound to its processor, ready to declare sink(s) with CausalProcessedStream.to(String) and then terminate the topology with CausalProcessedStream.build().
    CausalStream<K,V> - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    One or more causal source topics, ready to feed a single causal-decorated processor with CausalStream.process(ProcessorSupplier).
    CausalStreams - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    The causal application runtime: a Facade (GoF) over the Kafka Streams instance a CausalTopology runs as, and the causal machinery a plain KafkaStreams doesn't know about — graceful causal drain on shutdown, and (when configured) topology-epoch coordination — behind the one simple start/close lifecycle below.
    CausalStreams(CausalTopology, Properties) - Constructor for class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreams
    Assembles topology into a real Kafka Streams topology and wraps a KafkaStreams instance over it.
    CausalStreamsBuilder - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    Builds a CausalTopology: exactly one causal stage — a set of source topics feeding a causal-decorated processor and forwarding to one or more sinks.
    CausalStreamsBuilder() - Constructor for class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreamsBuilder
     
    CausalTopology - Class in io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
    The immutable causal topology CausalStreamsBuilder.build() produces: every declared stage's source topics, processor, sink(s), and partitioner.
    close() - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreams
    Gracefully shuts down: waits — unbounded, no timeout — for every task's causal buffer to drain through the ordinary delivery path, then, if coordination is configured, permanently decommissions this instance's members from the epoch domain, then stops the underlying KafkaStreams, then closes the coordination runtime.

    M

    merge(CausalDependencies) - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalDependencies
    Returns the causal union of these dependencies and other — the per-coordinate maximum offset.
    merge(CausalStream) - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStream
    Combines this stream's source topics with other's into one, so a later CausalStream.process(ProcessorSupplier) call fans every topic from both into the same causal stage.

    O

    observe(ConsumerRecord) - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalDependencies
    Folds a consumed record into these dependencies and returns the result: the union of these dependencies, the dependencies record itself carried, and record's own position (topic, partition, offset).

    P

    process(String, ProcessorSupplier) - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStream
    As CausalStream.process(ProcessorSupplier), naming the stage explicitly — the name becomes the causal buffer store's namespace, so give it a stable, unique name across topology edits and restarts rather than relying on the auto-derived default.
    process(ProcessorSupplier) - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStream
    Binds this stream's source topics to one causal-decorated processor.

    W

    withPartitioner(StreamPartitioner) - Method in class io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalProcessedStream
    Sets the StreamPartitioner applied to every sink this stage declares (default: Kafka's own key-hash partitioner) — never configurable per-sink, so two sinks in the same stage can never drift onto different partitioners.
